verdict.rationale: Unity supports automation-depth through Editor scripting APIs, custom Editor Windows/inspectors, AssetDatabase, and CLI/batch-mode tooling (unity-docs-6/7/8/10/11/25/26, unity-probe-rt-4) that a developer could use to script bulk asset or scene operations, and the new experimental Unity CLI adds structured JSON/TSV output and `unity eval` for direct Editor automation. However, no evidence documents a purpose-built 'bulk operation' feature (e.g., batch-apply to many selected assets/objects at once) — it must be hand-rolled via scripting rather than a first-class AI-native bulk-action capability. Missing for 10: explicit bulk-operation API/tool documentation, evidence of an agent performing bulk edits across many items, independent hands-on confirmation.
